stem.en: Oxygen has 8 protons. Sulphur, directly below it, has 16. Kabir says sulphur must pull harder, "because sixteen is more than eight". Which is right?

text.en: Oxygen pulls harder. Sulphur's outer electrons sit in a third shell, further out and shielded by more inner electrons, so the extra protons are more than cancelled.

feedback.en: Protons matter, but distance matters more. Sulphur's outer shell is a whole shell further from its nucleus.

text.en: They pull the same, because they are in the same column.

feedback.en: Same family means the same number of outer electrons. Going down the column, the pull drops.

text.en: Neither pulls; only chlorine and fluorine do.

feedback.en: Oxygen is the third-strongest puller in the whole table. It is why burning happens.

explanation.en: Down a column the atom gets bigger. The outer electrons are further from the nucleus and behind more shells, so the pull on them is weaker, whatever the proton count.
